label.en: ● Strict Monotonicity & The Inverse Function Theorem
label.ar: ● Strict Monotonicity & The Inverse الدالة مبرهنة

body.en:
A function \(f\) has an inverse \(f^{-1}\) if and only if \(f\) is one-to-one (injective) — meaning distinct inputs produce distinct outputs:

\[ x_1 \neq x_2 \implies f(x_1) \neq f(x_2). \]

Theorem (Monotonicity Criterion): If a continuous function \(f\) is strictly increasing or strictly decreasing on an interval \(I\), then \(f\) passes the Horizontal Line Test and is guaranteed to possess a unique continuous inverse function \(f^{-1}\) defined on \(f(I)\).

Fundamental Cancellation Identities:

\[ f(f^{-1}(x)) = x \quad \text{for all } x \in \text{Domain}(f^{-1}) = \text{Range}(f). \]\[ f^{-1}(f(x)) = x \quad \text{for all } x \in \text{Domain}(f) = \text{Range}(f^{-1}). \]

Geometric Reflection: The point \((a, b)\) lies on the graph of \(y = f(x)\) if and only if the reflected point \((b, a)\) lies on the graph of \(y = f^{-1}(x)\). The graph of \(f^{-1}\) is the exact reflection of the graph of \(f\) across the identity line \(y = x\).
body.ar:
A الدالة \(f\) has an inverse \(f^{-1}\) if and only if \(f\) is one-to-one (injective) — meaning distinct inputs produce distinct outputs:

\[ x_1 \neq x_2 \implies f(x_1) \neq f(x_2). \]

Theorem (Monotonicity Criterion): If a continuous الدالة \(f\) is strictly increasing or strictly decreasing on an interval \(I\), then \(f\) passes the Horizontal Line Test and is guaranteed to possess a unique continuous inverse الدالة \(f^{-1}\) defined on \(f(I)\).

Fundamental Cancellation المتطابقات:

\[ f(f^{-1}(x)) = x \quad \text{for all } x \in \text{Domain}(f^{-1}) = \text{Range}(f). \]\[ f^{-1}(f(x)) = x \quad \text{for all } x \in \text{Domain}(f) = \text{Range}(f^{-1}). \]

Geometric Reflection: The point \((a, b)\) lies on the التمثيل البياني of \(y = f(x)\) if and only if the reflected point \((b, a)\) lies on the التمثيل البياني of \(y = f^{-1}(x)\). The التمثيل البياني of \(f^{-1}\) is the exact reflection of the التمثيل البياني of \(f\) across the المتطابقة line \(y = x\).

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Unit 4 · Parameters, Vectors, and Matrices)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (Unit 4 · المعاملات, المتجهات, and المصفوفات)

body.en:
Why Orthogonal Projection & Eigenvalue Characteristic Equations Work: Decompose \(\mathbf{u} = c\mathbf{v} + \mathbf{w}\) where \(\mathbf{w} \perp \mathbf{v}\). Taking the dot product with \(\mathbf{v}\) uses \(\mathbf{w}\cdot\mathbf{v} = 0\) to isolate \(c\):

\[ \mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v} = c(\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{v}) + 0 \implies c = \frac{\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}}{\|\mathbf{v}\|^2} \]

For eigenvalues, \(A\mathbf{v} = \lambda\mathbf{v}\) with \(\mathbf{v} \ne \mathbf{0}\) is equivalent to \((A - \lambda I)\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{0}\). A homogeneous linear system has a non-trivial nullspace vector \(\mathbf{v} \ne \mathbf{0}\) if and only if the matrix \(A - \lambda I\) is singular, yielding the characteristic polynomial \(\det(A - \lambda I) = 0\).
body.ar:
Why Orthogonal Projection & Eigenvalue Characteristic المعادلات Work: Decompose \(\mathbf{u} = c\mathbf{v} + \mathbf{w}\) حيث \(\mathbf{w} \perp \mathbf{v}\). Taking the dot product with \(\mathbf{v}\) uses \(\mathbf{w}\cdot\mathbf{v} = 0\) to isolate \(c\):

\[ \mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v} = c(\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{v}) + 0 \implies c = \frac{\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}}{\|\mathbf{v}\|^2} \]

For القيم الذاتية, \(A\mathbf{v} = \lambda\mathbf{v}\) with \(\mathbf{v} \ne \mathbf{0}\) is equivalent to \((A - \lambda I)\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{0}\). A homogeneous linear system has a non-trivial nullspace المتجه \(\mathbf{v} \ne \mathbf{0}\) if and only if the المصفوفة \(A - \lambda I\) is singular, yielding the characteristic كثيرة الحدود \(\det(A - \lambda I) = 0\).

body.en:
Find the inverse function \(f^{-1}(x)\) for the rational function \(f(x) = \frac{4x - 5}{2x + 3}\), state its domain and range, and verify algebraically that \(f(f^{-1}(x)) = x\).

Step 1 (Solve for x): Let \(y = \frac{4x - 5}{2x + 3}\). Swap \(x\) and \(y\):

\[ x = \frac{4y - 5}{2y + 3} \implies x(2y + 3) = 4y - 5 \implies 2xy + 3x = 4y - 5. \]\[ 2xy - 4y = -3x - 5 \implies y(2x - 4) = -(3x + 5) \implies y = \frac{3x + 5}{4 - 2x}. \]\[ f^{-1}(x) = \frac{3x + 5}{4 - 2x}. \]

Step 2 (Domain and Range):

  • \(\text{Domain of } f = \{x \in \mathbb{R} \mid x \neq -3/2\} = \text{Range of } f^{-1}\).
  • \(\text{Domain of } f^{-1} = \{x \in \mathbb{R} \mid x \neq 2\} = \text{Range of } f\).

Step 3 (Composition Verification):

\[ f(f^{-1}(x)) = \frac{4\left(\frac{3x+5}{4-2x}\right) - 5}{2\left(\frac{3x+5}{4-2x}\right) + 3} = \frac{4(3x+5) - 5(4-2x)}{2(3x+5) + 3(4-2x)} = \frac{12x + 20 - 20 + 10x}{6x + 10 + 12 - 6x} = \frac{22x}{22} = x. \quad \checkmark \]
body.ar:
Find the inverse الدالة \(f^{-1}(x)\) for the rational الدالة \(f(x) = \frac{4x - 5}{2x + 3}\), state its المجال and المدى, and verify algebraically that \(f(f^{-1}(x)) = x\).

Step 1 (أوجد قيمة x): Let \(y = \frac{4x - 5}{2x + 3}\). Swap \(x\) and \(y\):

\[ x = \frac{4y - 5}{2y + 3} \implies x(2y + 3) = 4y - 5 \implies 2xy + 3x = 4y - 5. \]\[ 2xy - 4y = -3x - 5 \implies y(2x - 4) = -(3x + 5) \implies y = \frac{3x + 5}{4 - 2x}. \]\[ f^{-1}(x) = \frac{3x + 5}{4 - 2x}. \]

Step 2 (المجال and المدى):

  • \(\text{Domain of } f = \{x \in \mathbb{R} \mid x \neq -3/2\} = \text{Range of } f^{-1}\).
  • \(\text{Domain of } f^{-1} = \{x \in \mathbb{R} \mid x \neq 2\} = \text{Range of } f\).

Step 3 (Composition Verification):

\[ f(f^{-1}(x)) = \frac{4\left(\frac{3x+5}{4-2x}\right) - 5}{2\left(\frac{3x+5}{4-2x}\right) + 3} = \frac{4(3x+5) - 5(4-2x)}{2(3x+5) + 3(4-2x)} = \frac{12x + 20 - 20 + 10x}{6x + 10 + 12 - 6x} = \frac{22x}{22} = x. \quad \checkmark \]

body.en:
Problem (Hard): A vector \( \mathbf{v} \) is defined by its initial point \( P = (-5, 3) \) and its terminal point \( Q = (4, -2) \). What is the component form of vector \( \mathbf{v} \)?

Step-by-Step Solution: The component form of a vector \( \mathbf{v} \) directed from an initial point \( P = (x_1, y_1) \) to a terminal point \( Q = (x_2, y_2) \) is given by \( \mathbf{v} = \langle x_2 - x_1, y_2 - y_1 \rangle \). In this case, the initial point is \( P = (-5, 3) \) and the terminal point is \( Q = (4, -2) \). Therefore, the component form of \( \mathbf{v} \) is: \( \mathbf{v} = \langle 4 - (-5), -2 - 3 \rangle = \langle 4 + 5, -5 \rangle = \langle 9, -5 \rangle \).
body.ar:
Problem (Hard): A المتجه \( \mathbf{v} \) is defined by its initial point \( P = (-5, 3) \) and its terminal point \( Q = (4, -2) \). What is the component form of المتجه \( \mathbf{v} \)?

Step-by-Step الحل: The component form of a المتجه \( \mathbf{v} \) directed from an initial point \( P = (x_1, y_1) \) to a terminal point \( Q = (x_2, y_2) \) is المعطيات by \( \mathbf{v} = \langle x_2 - x_1, y_2 - y_1 \rangle \). In this case, the initial point is \( P = (-5, 3) \) and the terminal point is \( Q = (4, -2) \). وبالتالي, the component form of \( \mathbf{v} \) is: \( \mathbf{v} = \langle 4 - (-5), -2 - 3 \rangle = \langle 4 + 5, -5 \rangle = \langle 9, -5 \rangle \).

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

Consider the restricted quadratic function \(g(x) = 2(x - 3)^2 + 5\) defined on the domain \([3, \infty)\). Explain why \(g\) is invertible on this domain, find the formula for \(g^{-1}(x)\), and state the domain of \(g^{-1}\).
question.ar:
Level 1 · Foundations

Consider the restricted quadratic function \(g(x) = 2(x - 3)^2 + 5\) defined on the domain \([3, \infty)\). Explain why \(g\) is invertible on this domain, أوجد formula for \(g^{-1}(x)\), and state the domain of \(g^{-1}\).

solution.en:
Invertibility Justification: The vertex of the parabola is at \((3, 5)\). On \([3, \infty)\), \(g(x)\) is strictly increasing and therefore one-to-one, satisfying the horizontal line test.

Find Inverse Formula: Set \(y = 2(x - 3)^2 + 5\) for \(x \ge 3\):

\[ x = 2(y - 3)^2 + 5 \implies x - 5 = 2(y - 3)^2 \implies (y - 3)^2 = \frac{x - 5}{2}. \]

Taking the positive square root because \(y \ge 3\):

\[ y - 3 = \sqrt{\frac{x - 5}{2}} \implies g^{-1}(x) = 3 + \sqrt{\frac{x - 5}{2}}. \]

Domain of \(g^{-1}\): The range of \(g\) is \([5, \infty)\), so the domain of \(g^{-1}\) is \([5, \infty)\).

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Medium — Parametric Curves, Kinematics & 2D Vector Dot Products

body.en: Eliminate parameters to identify planar trajectories, model particle kinematics, and calculate vector magnitudes, directions, and dot products.
body.ar: Eliminate المعاملات to identify planar trajectories, model particle kinematics, and احسب المتجه magnitudes, directions, and dot products.

body.en:
A parametric curve in the plane is given by two coordinate functions \(x = f(t)\) and \(y = g(t)\) where \(t\) is the parameter over interval \(t \in [t_{\min}, t_{\max}]\). Unlike Cartesian relations, parametric representations preserve the speed, direction of motion, and time history of a moving object.

Elimination Techniques:

  1. Direct Substitution: Solve \(x = f(t)\) for \(t\) and substitute into \(y = g(t)\). (e.g. \(x = 2t + 1 \implies t = \frac{x-1}{2} \implies y = g\left(\frac{x-1}{2}\right)\)).
  2. Trigonometric Identity Elimination: Isolate \(\cos t\) and \(\sin t\) and use \(\cos^2 t + \sin^2 t = 1\): \[ x = h + a\cos t, \; y = k + b\sin t \implies \left(\frac{x - h}{a}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{y - k}{b}\right)^2 = 1 \quad (\text{Ellipse}). \]
  3. Hyperbolic / Secant-Tangent Elimination: Use \(\sec^2 t - \tan^2 t = 1\) for hyperbolas.
body.ar:
A parametric curve in the plane is المعطيات by two الإحداثي الدوال \(x = f(t)\) and \(y = g(t)\) حيث \(t\) is the المعامل over interval \(t \in [t_{\min}, t_{\max}]\). Unlike Cartesian relations, parametric representations preserve the speed, direction of motion, and time history of a moving object.

Elimination Techniques:

  1. Direct Substitution: Solve \(x = f(t)\) for \(t\) and عوّض into \(y = g(t)\). (e.g. \(x = 2t + 1 \implies t = \frac{x-1}{2} \implies y = g\left(\frac{x-1}{2}\right)\)).
  2. Trigonometric المتطابقة Elimination: Isolate \(\cos t\) and \(\sin t\) and use \(\cos^2 t + \sin^2 t = 1\): \[ x = h + a\cos t, \; y = k + b\sin t \implies \left(\frac{x - h}{a}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{y - k}{b}\right)^2 = 1 \quad (\text{Ellipse}). \]
  3. Hyperbolic / Secant-Tangent Elimination: Use \(\sec^2 t - \tan^2 t = 1\) for hyperbolas.

body.en:
Theorem: For non-zero vectors \(\vec{u} = \langle u_1, u_2 \rangle\) and \(\vec{v} = \langle v_1, v_2 \rangle\) with angle \(\theta\) between them:

\[ \vec{u} \cdot \vec{v} = u_1 v_1 + u_2 v_2 = |\vec{u}| |\vec{v}| \cos\theta. \]

Proof from the Law of Cosines:

Place vectors \(\vec{u}\) and \(\vec{v}\) tail-to-tail at the origin. The displacement vector connecting their heads is \(\vec{w} = \vec{u} - \vec{v} = \langle u_1 - v_1, u_2 - v_2 \rangle\). Applying the Law of Cosines to the triangle formed by these vectors:

\[ |\vec{u} - \vec{v}|^2 = |\vec{u}|^2 + |\vec{v}|^2 - 2|\vec{u}||\vec{v}|\cos\theta. \]

Expand the left side using components:

\[ (u_1 - v_1)^2 + (u_2 - v_2)^2 = (u_1^2 + u_2^2) + (v_1^2 + v_2^2) - 2(u_1 v_1 + u_2 v_2). \]\[ |\vec{u}|^2 + |\vec{v}|^2 - 2(u_1 v_1 + u_2 v_2) = |\vec{u}|^2 + |\vec{v}|^2 - 2|\vec{u}||\vec{v}|\cos\theta. \]

Cancelling \(|\vec{u}|^2 + |\vec{v}|^2\) and dividing by \(-2\) yields:

\[ u_1 v_1 + u_2 v_2 = |\vec{u}||\vec{v}|\cos\theta. \quad \blacksquare \]

Orthogonality Test: Two non-zero vectors are perpendicular (orthogonal) if and only if \(\vec{u} \cdot \vec{v} = 0\), because \(\cos(90^\circ) = 0\).
body.ar:
Theorem: For non-zero المتجهات \(\vec{u} = \langle u_1, u_2 \rangle\) and \(\vec{v} = \langle v_1, v_2 \rangle\) with الزاوية \(\theta\) between them:

\[ \vec{u} \cdot \vec{v} = u_1 v_1 + u_2 v_2 = |\vec{u}| |\vec{v}| \cos\theta. \]

Proof from the Law of Cosines:

Place المتجهات \(\vec{u}\) and \(\vec{v}\) tail-to-tail at the origin. The displacement المتجه connecting their heads is \(\vec{w} = \vec{u} - \vec{v} = \langle u_1 - v_1, u_2 - v_2 \rangle\). Applying the Law of Cosines to the المثلث formed by these المتجهات:

\[ |\vec{u} - \vec{v}|^2 = |\vec{u}|^2 + |\vec{v}|^2 - 2|\vec{u}||\vec{v}|\cos\theta. \]

Expand the left side using components:

\[ (u_1 - v_1)^2 + (u_2 - v_2)^2 = (u_1^2 + u_2^2) + (v_1^2 + v_2^2) - 2(u_1 v_1 + u_2 v_2). \]\[ |\vec{u}|^2 + |\vec{v}|^2 - 2(u_1 v_1 + u_2 v_2) = |\vec{u}|^2 + |\vec{v}|^2 - 2|\vec{u}||\vec{v}|\cos\theta. \]

Cancelling \(|\vec{u}|^2 + |\vec{v}|^2\) and dividing by \(-2\) yields:

\[ u_1 v_1 + u_2 v_2 = |\vec{u}||\vec{v}|\cos\theta. \quad \blacksquare \]

Orthogonality Test: Two non-zero المتجهات are perpendicular (orthogonal) if and only if \(\vec{u} \cdot \vec{v} = 0\), because \(\cos(90^\circ) = 0\).

label.en: ▲ AP Exam Traps & Pitfalls — Parameters, Vectors & Matrices
label.ar: ▲ AP Exam Traps & Pitfalls — المعاملات, المتجهات & المصفوفات

body.en:
• Direction of Motion in Parametric Equations: Eliminating the parameter gives the geometric shape (e.g. \(y = x^2\)), but discards direction of motion and domain boundaries. Always evaluate points at increasing \(t\) to determine if motion is left-to-right, right-to-left, or bounded on a segment.
  • Matrix Multiplication Non-Commutativity: In general, \(A B \neq B A\). When transforming a vector \(\vec{v}\) by matrix \(M\), write \(M \vec{v}\) (matrix on the left, column vector on the right).
  • Vector Angle Quadrant Ambiguity: When calculating direction angle \(\theta = \arctan(v_y / v_x)\), standard calculator outputs only give values in \((-\pi/2, \pi/2)\). If \(v_x < 0\), you must add \(\pi\) radians (or 180°) to place \(\theta\) in Quadrant II or III.
  • Singular Matrices & Area Collapse: A \(2 \times 2\) matrix is invertible if and only if \(\det(A) = ad - bc \neq 0\). If \(\det(A) = 0\), the transformation collapses the 2D plane into a 1D line or point (transformed area = 0).
body.ar:
• Direction of Motion in Parametric المعادلات: Eliminating the المعامل gives the geometric shape (e.g. \(y = x^2\)), but discards direction of motion and المجال boundaries. Always احسب قيمة points at increasing \(t\) to determine if motion is left-to-right, right-to-left, or bounded on a segment.
  • Matrix Multiplication Non-Commutativity: In general, \(A B \neq B A\). عندما transforming a المتجه \(\vec{v}\) by المصفوفة \(M\), write \(M \vec{v}\) (المصفوفة on the left, column المتجه on the right).
  • Vector الزاوية Quadrant Ambiguity: عندما calculating direction الزاوية \(\theta = \arctan(v_y / v_x)\), standard calculator outputs only give values in \((-\pi/2, \pi/2)\). If \(v_x < 0\), you must add \(\pi\) radians (or 180°) to place \(\theta\) in Quadrant II or III.
  • Singular المصفوفات & المساحة Collapse: A \(2 \times 2\) المصفوفة is invertible if and only if \(\det(A) = ad - bc \neq 0\). If \(\det(A) = 0\), the transformation collapses the 2D plane into a 1D line or point (transformed المساحة = 0).

body.en:
A projectile launched from an elevated cliff has position given by the parametric equations \(x(t) = 30t\) and \(y(t) = 45 + 40t - 5t^2\), where \(t \ge 0\) is in seconds and distances are in meters. (a) Eliminate the parameter to find the Cartesian equation of the trajectory. (b) Find the time \(t\) when the projectile strikes the ground (\(y = 0\)), and find its horizontal landing distance.

Part (a): Solve \(x(t)\) for \(t\): \[ t = \frac{x}{30}. \] Substitute into \(y(t)\): \[ y = 45 + 40\left(\frac{x}{30}\right) - 5\left(\frac{x}{30}\right)^2 = 45 + \frac{4}{3}x - 5\left(\frac{x^2}{900}\right) = 45 + \frac{4}{3}x - \frac{x^2}{180}. \] This is a downward-opening parabola.

Part (b): Ground impact occurs when \(y(t) = 0\): \[ -5t^2 + 40t + 45 = 0 \implies t^2 - 8t - 9 = 0 \implies (t - 9)(t + 1) = 0. \] Since \(t \ge 0\), flight duration is \(t = \mathbf{9}\text{ seconds}\). Landing distance: \[ x(9) = 30(9) = \mathbf{270}\text{ meters}. \]
body.ar:
A projectile launched from an elevated cliff has position المعطيات by the parametric المعادلات \(x(t) = 30t\) and \(y(t) = 45 + 40t - 5t^2\), حيث \(t \ge 0\) is in seconds and distances are in meters. (a) Eliminate the المعامل to أوجد Cartesian المعادلة of the trajectory. (b) أوجد time \(t\) عندما the projectile strikes the ground (\(y = 0\)), and find its horizontal landing distance.

Part (a): Solve \(x(t)\) for \(t\): \[ t = \frac{x}{30}. \] عوّض into \(y(t)\): \[ y = 45 + 40\left(\frac{x}{30}\right) - 5\left(\frac{x}{30}\right)^2 = 45 + \frac{4}{3}x - 5\left(\frac{x^2}{900}\right) = 45 + \frac{4}{3}x - \frac{x^2}{180}. \] This is a downward-opening parabola.

Part (b): Ground impact occurs عندما \(y(t) = 0\): \[ -5t^2 + 40t + 45 = 0 \implies t^2 - 8t - 9 = 0 \implies (t - 9)(t + 1) = 0. \] Since \(t \ge 0\), flight duration is \(t = \mathbf{9}\text{ seconds}\). Landing distance: \[ x(9) = 30(9) = \mathbf{270}\text{ meters}. \]

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

Vector \(\vec{u} = \langle 4, -3 \rangle\) and vector \(\vec{v} = \langle 1, 7 \rangle\). Calculate the magnitude of each vector, determine the dot product \(\vec{u} \cdot \vec{v}\), and find the exact angle \(\theta\) between them in radians.
question.ar:
Level 2 · Medium

Vector \(\vec{u} = \langle 4, -3 \rangle\) and vector \(\vec{v} = \langle 1, 7 \rangle\). احسب magnitude of each vector, حدّد dot product \(\vec{u} \cdot \vec{v}\), and أوجد exact angle \(\theta\) between them in radians.

solution.ar:
خطوات الحل التفصيلية:

Magnitudes:

\[ |\vec{u}| = \sqrt{4^2 + (-3)^2} = \sqrt{16 + 9} = \sqrt{25} = 5. \]\[ |\vec{v}| = \sqrt{1^2 + 7^2} = \sqrt{1 + 49} = \sqrt{50} = 5\sqrt{2}. \]

Dot Product:

\[ \vec{u} \cdot \vec{v} = (4)(1) + (-3)(7) = 4 - 21 = -17. \]

Angle Between Vectors: Use \(\cos\theta = \frac{\vec{u} \cdot \vec{v}}{|\vec{u}||\vec{v}|}\):

\[ \cos\theta = \frac{-17}{(5)(5\sqrt{2})} = \frac{-17}{25\sqrt{2}} = \frac{-17\sqrt{2}}{50} \approx -0.48083. \]\[ \theta = \arccos\left(\frac{-17\sqrt{2}}{50}\right) \approx \mathbf{2.072}\text{ radians} \quad (\approx 118.7^\circ). \]

hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(|\vec{u}| = \sqrt{4^2 + (-3)^2} = \sqrt{16 + 9} = \sqrt{25}\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Rewrite and simplify to obtain: \(|\vec{v}| = \sqrt{1^2 + 7^2} = \sqrt{1 + 49} = \sqrt{50} = 5\sqrt{2}\) Dot Product: \(\vec{u} \cdot \vec{v} = (4)(1) + (-3)(7) = 4 - 21\).
hints.ar: أعد كتابة العلاقة وبسّطها للحصول على: \(|\vec{v}| = \sqrt{1^2 + 7^2} = \sqrt{1 + 49} = \sqrt{50} = 5\sqrt{2}\) Dot Product: \(\vec{u} \cdot \vec{v} = (4)(1) + (-3)(7) = 4 - 21\).

hints.en: Use the resulting form to finish: \(\theta = \arccos\left(\frac{-17\sqrt{2}}{50}\right)\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(\theta = \arccos\left(\frac{-17\sqrt{2}}{50}\right)\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced — Matrix Linear Transformations, Determinant Area Scaling & Rotations

body.en: Apply 2x2 matrix representations to map geometric figures, prove the determinant area distortion theorem, and calculate rotation/reflection transformations.
body.ar: Apply 2x2 المصفوفة representations to map geometric figures, prove the المحدد المساحة distortion المبرهنة, and احسب rotation/reflection transformations.

body.en:
A linear transformation \(T: \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2\) maps vectors via matrix multiplication:

\[ T\begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} ax + by \\ cx + dy \end{pmatrix}. \]

Basis Representation: The columns of \(A\) are the transformed images of the standard basis vectors \(\vec{i} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(\vec{j} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}\):

\[ T(\vec{i}) = \begin{pmatrix} a \\ c \end{pmatrix}, \quad T(\vec{j}) = \begin{pmatrix} b \\ d \end{pmatrix}. \]

Determinant & Inverse Matrix:

\[ \det(A) = ad - bc. \]\[ A^{-1} = \frac{1}{ad - bc} \begin{pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{pmatrix} \quad (\text{provided } \det(A) \neq 0). \]
body.ar:
A linear transformation \(T: \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2\) maps المتجهات via المصفوفة multiplication:

\[ T\begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} ax + by \\ cx + dy \end{pmatrix}. \]

Basis Representation: The columns of \(A\) are the transformed images of the standard basis المتجهات \(\vec{i} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(\vec{j} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}\):

\[ T(\vec{i}) = \begin{pmatrix} a \\ c \end{pmatrix}, \quad T(\vec{j}) = \begin{pmatrix} b \\ d \end{pmatrix}. \]

Determinant & Inverse المصفوفة:

\[ \det(A) = ad - bc. \]\[ A^{-1} = \frac{1}{ad - bc} \begin{pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{pmatrix} \quad (\text{provided } \det(A) \neq 0). \]

label.en: ● Determinant Area Scaling Theorem & Rotation Matrices
label.ar: ● المحدد المساحة Scaling مبرهنة & Rotation المصفوفات

body.en:
Area Scaling Theorem: Let \(S\) be any planar region with finite area. When the matrix transformation \(T(\vec{x}) = A\vec{x}\) maps region \(S\) to its image \(T(S)\), the area is scaled by exactly the absolute value of the determinant:

\[ \text{Area}(T(S)) = |\det(A)| \cdot \text{Area}(S) = |ad - bc| \cdot \text{Area}(S). \]

Sign Meaning: If \(\det(A) > 0\), the transformation preserves spatial orientation (counterclockwise paths remain counterclockwise). If \(\det(A) < 0\), orientation is reversed (as in a reflection).

Rotation Matrix \(R(\theta)\): Counterclockwise rotation through angle \(\theta\) maps \(\vec{i} \mapsto \begin{pmatrix} \cos\theta \\ \sin\theta \end{pmatrix}\) and \(\vec{j} \mapsto \begin{pmatrix} -\sin\theta \\ \cos\theta \end{pmatrix}\):

\[ R(\theta) = \begin{pmatrix} \cos\theta & -\sin\theta \\ \sin\theta & \cos\theta \end{pmatrix}. \]

Notice that \(\det(R(\theta)) = (\cos\theta)(\cos\theta) - (-\sin\theta)(\sin\theta) = \cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1\), proving analytically that pure rotations preserve area identically without distortion.
body.ar:
Area Scaling مبرهنة: Let \(S\) be any planar region with finite المساحة. عندما the المصفوفة transformation \(T(\vec{x}) = A\vec{x}\) maps region \(S\) to its image \(T(S)\), the المساحة is scaled by exactly the absolute value of the المحدد:

\[ \text{Area}(T(S)) = |\det(A)| \cdot \text{Area}(S) = |ad - bc| \cdot \text{Area}(S). \]

Sign Meaning: If \(\det(A) > 0\), the transformation preserves spatial orientation (counterclockwise paths remain counterclockwise). If \(\det(A) < 0\), orientation is reversed (as in a reflection).

Rotation المصفوفة \(R(\theta)\): Counterclockwise rotation through الزاوية \(\theta\) maps \(\vec{i} \mapsto \begin{pmatrix} \cos\theta \\ \sin\theta \end{pmatrix}\) and \(\vec{j} \mapsto \begin{pmatrix} -\sin\theta \\ \cos\theta \end{pmatrix}\):

\[ R(\theta) = \begin{pmatrix} \cos\theta & -\sin\theta \\ \sin\theta & \cos\theta \end{pmatrix}. \]

Notice that \(\det(R(\theta)) = (\cos\theta)(\cos\theta) - (-\sin\theta)(\sin\theta) = \cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1\), proving analytically that pure rotations preserve المساحة identically without distortion.

body.en:
A triangle in the plane has vertices \(P(0, 0)\), \(Q(4, 0)\), and \(R(2, 3)\). The linear transformation matrix \(M = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & -1 \\ 2 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\) maps the triangle to a new image triangle \(P'Q'R'\). (a) Calculate the area of the original triangle. (b) Find \(\det(M)\) and the inverse matrix \(M^{-1}\). (c) Determine the coordinates of \(Q'\) and \(R'\), and calculate the area of the transformed triangle \(P'Q'R'\).

Part (a): The base along the \(x\)-axis is \(b = 4\) and altitude is \(h = 3\):

\[ \text{Area}(\triangle PQR) = \frac{1}{2} b h = \frac{1}{2}(4)(3) = \mathbf{6}\text{ square units}. \]

Part (b): Determinant of \(M\): \[ \det(M) = (3)(4) - (-1)(2) = 12 + 2 = \mathbf{14}. \] Inverse matrix: \[ M^{-1} = \frac{1}{14} \begin{pmatrix} 4 & 1 \\ -2 & 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2/7 & 1/14 \\ -1/7 & 3/14 \end{pmatrix}. \]

Part (c): Map coordinates:

\[ Q' = M\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3(4) + (-1)(0) \\ 2(4) + 4(0) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 12 \\ 8 \end{pmatrix} \implies Q'(12, 8). \]\[ R' = M\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3(2) + (-1)(3) \\ 2(2) + 4(3) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 16 \end{pmatrix} \implies R'(3, 16). \]

By the Area Scaling Theorem:

\[ \text{Area}(\triangle P'Q'R') = |\det(M)| \cdot \text{Area}(\triangle PQR) = 14 \times 6 = \mathbf{84}\text{ square units}. \]
body.ar:
A المثلث in the plane has vertices \(P(0, 0)\), \(Q(4, 0)\), and \(R(2, 3)\). The linear transformation المصفوفة \(M = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & -1 \\ 2 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\) maps the المثلث to a new image المثلث \(P'Q'R'\). (a) احسب المساحة of the original المثلث. (b) Find \(\det(M)\) and the inverse المصفوفة \(M^{-1}\). (c) حدّد الإحداثيات of \(Q'\) and \(R'\), and احسب المساحة of the transformed المثلث \(P'Q'R'\).

Part (a): The base along the \(x\)-axis is \(b = 4\) and altitude is \(h = 3\):

\[ \text{Area}(\triangle PQR) = \frac{1}{2} b h = \frac{1}{2}(4)(3) = \mathbf{6}\text{ square units}. \]

Part (b): المحدد of \(M\): \[ \det(M) = (3)(4) - (-1)(2) = 12 + 2 = \mathbf{14}. \] Inverse المصفوفة: \[ M^{-1} = \frac{1}{14} \begin{pmatrix} 4 & 1 \\ -2 & 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2/7 & 1/14 \\ -1/7 & 3/14 \end{pmatrix}. \]

Part (c): Map الإحداثيات:

\[ Q' = M\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3(4) + (-1)(0) \\ 2(4) + 4(0) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 12 \\ 8 \end{pmatrix} \implies Q'(12, 8). \]\[ R' = M\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3(2) + (-1)(3) \\ 2(2) + 4(3) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 16 \end{pmatrix} \implies R'(3, 16). \]

By the المساحة Scaling مبرهنة:

\[ \text{Area}(\triangle P'Q'R') = |\det(M)| \cdot \text{Area}(\triangle PQR) = 14 \times 6 = \mathbf{84}\text{ square units}. \]

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

Find the matrix \(R\) that rotates vectors by \(\theta = \frac{2\pi}{3}\) radians counterclockwise, and use it to find the image of the vector \(\vec{w} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}\). Verify that the magnitude of \(\vec{w}\) is preserved under the transformation.
question.ar:
Level 3 · Advanced

أوجد matrix \(R\) that rotates vectors by \(\theta = \frac{2\pi}{3}\) radians counterclockwise, and use it to أوجد image of the vector \(\vec{w} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}\). Verإذا كانy that the magnitude of \(\vec{w}\) is preserved under the transformation.

solution.en:
Step 1 (Formulate Rotation Matrix): For \(\theta = \frac{2\pi}{3}\): \(\cos(2\pi/3) = -\frac{1}{2}\) and \(\sin(2\pi/3) = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\):

\[ R = \begin{pmatrix} -1/2 & -\sqrt{3}/2 \\ \sqrt{3}/2 & -1/2 \end{pmatrix}. \]

Step 2 (Transform \(\vec{w}\)):

\[ R \vec{w} = \begin{pmatrix} -1/2 & -\sqrt{3}/2 \\ \sqrt{3}/2 & -1/2 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} (-1/2)(4) + (-\sqrt{3}/2)(-2) \\ (\sqrt{3}/2)(4) + (-1/2)(-2) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -2 + \sqrt{3} \\ 2\sqrt{3} + 1 \end{pmatrix}. \]

Step 3 (Verify Magnitude Preservation):

\[ |\vec{w}|^2 = 4^2 + (-2)^2 = 16 + 4 = 20. \]\[ |R\vec{w}|^2 = (-2 + \sqrt{3})^2 + (2\sqrt{3} + 1)^2 = (4 - 4\sqrt{3} + 3) + (12 + 4\sqrt{3} + 1) = 7 + 13 = 20. \]

Since \(|R\vec{w}|^2 = |\vec{w}|^2 = 20\), the magnitude is \(|\vec{w}| = \sqrt{20} = 2\sqrt{5}\) and is preserved identically.
